key_insight: This paper shows how generalization depends jointly on model width and training data in a feature-learning setting, extending scaling-law theory beyond fixed-feature or infinite-width assumptions. It identifies how increasing parameters and sample size interact in quadratic neural networks to shape test error.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of theory for joint width–data scaling laws in realistic feature-learning models, where generalization is not determined by data or compute alone. It fills the gap between classical fixed-feature analyses and practical neural networks with trainable representations.
method: Analyze ℓ2-regularized empirical test error in quadratic neural networks.
Study generalization as a function of both the number of trainable parameters and the number of samples.
Derive scaling-law behavior in a feature-learning regime rather than relying on infinite-width or online-SGD assumptions.
impact: This helps practitioners understand how to trade off model size and dataset size when designing and scaling neural networks. It can guide more efficient choices for training budget, architecture width, and data collection.
visual_elements: A two-axis scaling plot with width on one axis and data size on the other, showing test error contours.
A schematic of a quadratic neural network highlighting trainable features versus output layer parameters.
A comparison diagram between fixed-feature, infinite-width, and feature-learning regimes.
An infographic arrow showing how increasing width and data jointly reduce generalization error.
paper_title: How Width and Data Shape Generalization Scaling Laws in Quadratic Neural Networks
paper_authors: Julius Girardin, Emanuele Troiani, Yizhou Xu, Vittorio Erba, Florent Krzakala
